# Open differences between tests/fixtures/*/expected*.json (written by hand
# before the rules existed) and the engine, waiting for review. The expected
# files are never edited to match the engine; TestExpectedFindings passes
# only while the engine's differences are exactly these lines, so a new
# difference, or one that disappears, fails it.
#
# A - expected file omission: the paths rely on documented defaults
#     (DESIGN.md 4.7) that the hand-written files did not list:
#     eks.irsa.audience (no eks.amazonaws.com/audience annotation) and
#     eks.pod-identity.disableSessionTags.
# B - scenario 2: the decrypt grant uses StringEquals
#     kms:EncryptionContext:aws:s3:arn = the bucket ARN, which S3 sends only
#     with an S3 Bucket Key; without one the context is the object ARN
#     (S3 User Guide > Encryption context). No Bucket Key default is
#     documented, so the intended access is unconfirmed, not verified.
# C - scenarios 4 and 5: tools/debug runs as tools/default, which has no
#     eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn annotation, so its pods get no
#     sts.amazonaws.com token; STS checks the token audience against the
#     OIDC provider's client IDs whatever the trust says.
# D - scenario 14: the snapshot has no workload and the roles trust only
#     ec2.amazonaws.com, so no entry point reaches either role.
